## Problem

Scan and pair runs produce JSONL reports and probe transcripts.
Machine evidence is not a deliverable. The reader (a client, an IR
team, a later auditor) needs the assessment written up. The write-up
keeps the evidence intact through the hand-off. It states the run
conditions that make the run reproducible. It carries verbatim outputs
instead of paraphrases. It carries the mapping ids a reviewer checks
against the catalogue. The scaffold below carries all of that — from
the distribution's own reporting plan, not an ad-hoc folder of loose
files.

## Solution

`kailash report new` is **roadmap-stage**. The CLI ships it in the
spec's command surface, yet it lands per the roadmap (spec §6.2's
remaining KA-14 children). The report templates themselves are a
landed-report lane item. At the current tree `report-templates/` in
the OS repo is a stub. The grounded alternative TODAY: scaffold the
same structure directly with quarto. Kailash ships quarto at o-06 for
exactly this job. Quarto is also what the roadmap command wraps, per
the spec's report-template design. Pin the manifest hash the report
speaks against. The roadmap command's `repro/` dir encodes the same
pin discipline:

```bash
# 1. The direct scaffold (the landed path today):
mkdir -p my-assessment/findings my-assessment/evidence
cd my-assessment

#    _quarto.yml + index.qmd as below; findings are hand-written
#    pages under findings/<id>.qmd (the scaffold has no tool steps)

# 2. Pin the manifest the report speaks against (the repro contract):
kailash manifest check                       # -> {"categories": <n>, "tools": <n>}
cp "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v kailash)")")/../manifest/tools.yaml" \
   evidence/tools-pinned.yaml 2>/dev/null \
  || kailash info garak > evidence/garak-row-pinned.json
sha256sum evidence/*.yaml evidence/*.json > evidence/REPRO.sha256

# 3. Render to every delivery format (HTML for reading, PDF for hand-off):
quarto render index.qmd --to html
quarto render index.qmd --to pdf
```

The minimal `_quarto.yml` + `index.qmd` skeleton (the fields the
roadmap templates pre-structure):

```yaml
project:
  type: default
  output-dir: _render
format:
  html: {theme: cosmo, toc: true}
  pdf:  {documentclass: article}
```

```markdown
---
title: "LLM red-team assessment — <target system>"
author: "<operator>"
date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
---

## Scope + authorisation
<what was tested, on whose written authorisation — cite the
responsible-use statement's operator-responsibility clause>

## Method (reproducible conditions)
- tool + pin: garak <pin version> (kailash manifest hash <hash>)
- OWASP scope: LLM01 (both epochs per the manifest row)
- generations per probe: <g> · seed: <s>  ← the exact -g / -s values

## Findings
### <F-01> <one-line title>
- Class: OWASP LLM01 · ATLAS: AML.T0051
- Evidence: `findings/F-01.qmd` — the probe's VERBATIM exchange
  (prompt + response as captured), never a paraphrase
- Repro: the exact command line, the tool's own report file attached
  (e.g. garak_<ts>.jsonl, the probe-pair JSONL from the pair recipe)
```

What success looks like:

- `quarto render` exits 0. `_render/` holds the HTML (and PDF)
- the repro dir carries the pinned manifest row(s) + the checksum of
  the pin. Anyone can re-run the scan against the same pin and compare
  reports seed-for-seed
- every finding has an id, a class with its ATLAS/OWASP ids, and a
  verbatim evidence block — no finding relies on a paraphrase

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
pandoc
  to: html
  output-file: index.html
<render-time messages — shapes, not transcripts>
Output created: _render/index.html
```

## Discussion

- **Why the roadmap command still matters:** `kailash report new
  <type> <name>` scaffolds from the three declared engagement
  types — `llm-redteam`, `adversarial-ml`, `supply-chain-audit`. Each
  type carries its own `_quarto.yml`, a pre-structured `index.qmd`,
  `findings/` stubs, and a `repro/` manifest-hash pin (spec §5.4).
  When it lands, it replaces steps 1–2 with one command against a
  kept-in-sync template. Verify the landed template's shape at that
  point, not this recipe's hand scaffold. Check the
  [CLI inventory recipe](kailash-cli-manifest-inventory.html) for
  what is landed when.
- **What the report MUST carry (and why):** the verbatim outputs
  carry the evidence discipline. The book's no-invented-evidence rule
  applies to reports too. The pair recipe's ATTEMPTED/ok/FAIL +
  record-verbatim contract states the same principle. The ATLAS ids
  (`AML.T####` from the manifest row) keep a finding checkable
  against the catalogue. The seed + generation values make the
  post-config-change diff meaningful. Without them, the
  "did it move" question is unanswerable.
- **The responsible-use clause inside the report:** the OS's
  responsible-use statement makes the operator's authorisation a
  named responsibility. An assessment report that omits who
  authorised the work against what target leaves the legal frame off
  the record. The statement itself ships in the distribution (MOTD,
  `kailash doctor` output, Layer-ATTACK pages). Cite it, and link
  the written authorisation in the scope section.
- **Seed the report from the machine, not the memory:** the Method
  section's values come from the run's own artefacts. The sources:
  the tool's banner line (version), the JSONL report (probe set,
  generations), `kailash info <tool>` (the mapping ids, the licence).
  Never retype values from recollection. This mirrors the probe-pair
  recipe's record discipline on the report side.
- **Format choice:** the a-02 scan recipes produce JSONL. If the
  deliverable must chain into a ticket or a review workflow, attach
  BOTH the JSONL and the rendered HTML — the first is the evidence,
  the second is the reading surface.
- **texlive is opt-in:** the PDF leg needs a LaTeX toolchain. On a
  default image, texlive rides the opt-in `kailash-data.*` lane (see
  [data packs](../admin/data-packs.html)). The alternative: the HTML
  leg renders alone.
